title: WhoSampled
why: The user-built database of samples, covers and remixes; owned by Spotify since November 2025.

title: Tracklib, The State of Sampling
why: Chart-level counts of how much hit music samples and from which decades. A company report from a seller of licensed samples.

title: Kembrew McLeod's interview with Chuck D and Hank Shocklee
why: Chuck D and Hank Shocklee make the argument, in their own words, that clearance changed how hip-hop sounds.

title: Creative License: The Law and Culture of Digital Sampling (Kembrew McLeod and Peter DiCola, Duke University Press, 2011) - excerpt
why: Chapter 1 of the fullest account of what clearance costs and what it did to dense sample records.

title: Wayne Marshall and Jayson Beaster-Jones, 'It takes a little lawsuit'
why: Scholarship on the 'Addictive' case and Bollywood samples in US pop, by a leading writer on dembow's Jamaican roots.

title: Smithsonian Anthology of Hip-Hop and Rap (Smithsonian Folkways / NMAAHC, 2021)
why: 129 tracks and a 300-page book; some of the songs chosen for it could not be licensed.

title: US Copyright Office, Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
why: The Office's three-part report on digital replicas, copyrightability of AI output and AI training.

title: Complete Music Update
why: Trade coverage that follows the dembow case and the label deals with AI music companies closely.
